messages:
Jordan: FYI: canary run for raven-lite-int8 is showing a spike in toolcall JSON parse failures when TTL/backoff combo is tight. logs attached below.
Sam: ok can you paste a minimal example?
Jordan: sure — sample payload we got back from model: `{"tool":"search","args":[{"q":"safety policies"}`  <--- missing closing bracket/brace, appears truncated mid-token.
Nina: this is that partial streaming/early-terminate symptom we saw before with smaller KV cache + quant noise. when the model emits partial tokens right before the request TTL fires, our client finishes the connection and we hand an incomplete stream to the parser.
Lee: is TTL on our side (agent) or the customer's request-level timeout?
Jordan: agent enforced TTL (the one in route config) currently set to 150ms for canary to catch slow tails. also backoff retry window is 250ms. the interplay seems to make quick second attempts that reattach to a different model replica and we sometimes see concatenated fragments.
Sam: concatenated fragments as in: `...\"args\":[{\"q\":\"safety\"}` + `\"policies\"}]}` -> resulting in `...\"q\":\"safety\"} \"policies\"...]` which obviously breaks JSON.
Maria: CI-Bot posted the raw canary run few mins ago:
CI-Bot: canary/raven-lite-int8 #42 finished: 37/500 parse_failures, median latency 92ms, p99 312ms, retry_rate 6.2%
Nina: numbers line up with TTL evictions triggering retries and the second replica not always sending a clean sentence boundary. quantized tokenization makes EOS/commas appear different length.
Lee: hypothesis: short TTL + aggressive retry creates stream splicing where the first stream is cut mid-token and the second response starts without a separator. parser gets one concatenated chunk that is invalid.
Sam: quick mitigation idea: when a retry happens, inject a safe separator token before accepting the new stream (e.g., newline + "__SEAM__"), then our JSON-repair heuristic can detect seam and attempt to stitch safely.
Jordan: I like that for a short-term patch. longer term we should: increase TTL to 250ms for int8 canaries, add seam injection on retry, and improve json-repair heuristics (strip trailing commas, attempt NDJSON fallback).
Maria: can we reproduce locally? steps?
Jordan: repro script: `./scripts/canary_run.sh --model raven-lite-int8 --seed 42 --requests 1000 --timeout 150` then tail the logs: `grep PARSE_FAIL canary.log | head`. I'll add the exact log snippet to the run.
Sam: also add a check in postprocess: if parse fails and the raw text contains multiple top-level `{` braces, try NDJSON split and pick the last full object. fallback should be opt-in per-route.
Nina: note: NDJSON fallback may mask real semantic truncations for toolcall arrays. we need to record telemetry when fallback used so quality team can inspect.
Lee: action items: Jordan increase canary TTL to 250ms (J), Sam implement seam injection on retry (S), Maria add telemetry flag for NDJSON-fallback uses (M), Nina write a quick eval comparing parse-correctness vs hallucination rate (N).
Jordan: I'll push a short CL for TTL change and repro logs now. expecting CI runs in ~20m.
CI-Bot: CL 4412 pushed to canary-config: TTL=250ms for raven-lite-int8.
Maria: ping when CI finishes. I'll add a dashboard tile for NDJSON-fallback counts.
Sam: prototype for seam injection is tiny: on retry write `\n__SEAM__\n` to the client stream before piping new bytes. if downstream sees `__SEAM__` treat as a boundary anchor. pushing draft now.
Nina: also let's record the model-replica-id in the parse-failure telemetry so we can correlate replicas with higher splice rates.
Jordan: agreed. final note: keep retry budget conservative during canary — we might be inflating failure signals.
Lee: thanks all. we'll regroup after CI. :thumbsup:
